_comment: Refold-and-validate config for the binder block. Each designed protein is folded WITH the target DNA duplex, so the fold predicts the protein-DNA complex and yields interface ipTM plus a per-token PAE.
_supersedes: This file previously specified a THREE-oracle comparison (protenix + openfold3 + esmfold2) run on the same designs, with a `{id, chains:[...]}` complex-JSON template. Both are obsolete as of 2026-08-06. The oracle question was settled by measurement instead of comparison-at-scale (analysis/oracle_controls/RESULTS.md), and the complex-JSON shape shown here was accepted by NO pecli oracle -- the four-oracle control panel established the real per-oracle shapes, and scripts/build_fold_inputs.py now emits the rf3 one.
_oracle_rationale: Measured over a natural-TF control panel (5 sequence-specific TFs, 1 non-specific duplex binder, 2 non-binders x 8 DNA targets), the metric of record being argmin -- does the panel-wide lowest minPAE land on each TF's own cognate site? rf3 4/5, protenix 2/5, openfold3 0/5, esmfold2 4/5. rf3 also has the only measured binder/non-binder separation (+9.12 A excl. TBP) and is the cheapest at $0.020/fold measured. protenix's binder and non-binder minPAE ranges OVERLAP (the non-specific binder Sac7d scores the lowest minPAE of any protein), and it emits no per-token PAE unless the run passes --need-atom-confidence true (pecli #173).
_esmfold2: The cross-check oracle, not the panel one: it ties rf3 on argmin, is better calibrated in absolute minPAE, and is the only oracle that models TBP at all -- but costs $0.22/fold, 10x rf3, because ~93% of its runtime is weight restore on a premium GPU tier (pecli #180, unresolved). Use it to spot-check top-ranked designs.
_scope_limit: The metric is validated for MAJOR-GROOVE readers, which is the mode rfd3na's ori-token + H-bond conditioning targets. TBP, a minor-groove reader that kinks DNA ~80 degrees, fails on rf3, protenix and openfold3 alike -- flagged as a stress test in curated_controls.json before any fold was run.
_templated: NEVER template this stage. The gate is a self-consistency check -- does the designed SEQUENCE independently fold back into the backbone it was designed for? -- so supplying that backbone as a template hands the fold the answer and collapses RMSD toward zero. The paper does not template here either; its only templated step is the specificity block's all-by-all.
_msa_free: Single-sequence a3m via the _pecli_rf3_msa_a3m carrier on the protein component. Scientific: de novo designs have no meaningful alignment. Financial: omitting any MSA makes pecli auto-route the fold to a PAID msa->rf3 pipeline, and `--use-msa false` does NOT suppress it (pecli #174).

input_shape._comment: Emitted by scripts/build_fold_inputs.py. rf3's top level is a LIST of {name, components}; a DNA strand is an ordinary sequence component distinguished by chain_type.
input_shape._chain_type_trap: chain_type is optional and otherwise inferred from the alphabet, but a DNA strand containing no T is inferred as RNA (the all-RNA branch is tested before the all-DNA branch) and would silently fold as RNA. It is always written explicitly.
input_shape._chain_order: protein A + DNA B,C -- the OPPOSITE of the relaxed rfd3na backbone (DNA A,B + protein C). That mismatch caused the Stage-7 RMSD bug; filter_binder_block.py now pairs DNA strands by base sequence rather than by chain id.

_sequences_per_backbone: The paper's depth, and the default. At scale, `build_fold_inputs.py --top-n-per-backbone 1` is the cost lever: refolding is 89% of a backbone's $0.112, so 1 seq/backbone quarters the first gate's cost. Justified by our own smoke-test measurement that per-backbone spread in major-groove H-bonds far exceeds within-backbone spread ([0,1,0,0,0] vs [13,0,13,0,7]) -- backbone quality dominates sequence choice. It IS a deviation from the paper; record it in docs/replication_log.md when used.

gates._comment: Paper Methods: fold -> DNA-aligned protein Ca-RMSD < 8 A -> LigandMPNN resample -> fold -> RMSD < 3 A, ipTM > 0.7, high H-bond counts. filter_binder_block.py --stage selects which; the ipTM gate is INACTIVE at pre_resample, so passing --iptm-gate there silently does nothing.

outputs._comment: scripts/filter_binder_block.py records, per design: DNA-aligned protein Ca-RMSD (design vs refold), protein-only Ca-RMSD (which decomposes a fold failure from a PLACEMENT failure -- the smoke test's dominant mode: 9/50 folded to <3 A protein-only but sat >8 A off after DNA alignment), ipTM, on-target minPAE, protein-DNA and major-groove H-bond counts, and runtime.
